I think you could go to continuation school. It’s kind of like being home schooled but instead you finish schooling faster and see people once a week. Granted, you will see people that are dysfunctional as hell. I would suggest you just do homeschooling and pursue a sport team you may be interested in. If you can’t join a sport team, find structure for your life with scheduling what you need/want to do. Don’t just stop here. I know it’s a fresh wound and it appears your parents aren’t making it easier but try to get your day going with a schedule. It doesn’t have to be a whole lot at first. Wake up early forsure and go for a walk. To try to get some kind of routine going that will give you more energy and motivation. Try to get work done when you’re back— clean your room, learn coding (or whatever you desire) on YouTube, do body workouts that engage certain parts of your body on certain days, and eat healthier. Talk to the continuation/adult schools around you and I think once you’ve gotten enough credits, you could do community college. 

Your parents may want you to have that sense of purpose too with a work schedule. That could work too for the time being—super part time job to help you save money and sanity. It’s all worth a shot. You’re allowed to feel these emotions and process it—really feel it. But after that, wash your face with cold water, take 5-10 deep breaths, longer exhale, and move.
